messages:
irene: Odd reproducible failure: our sampleapp built with Vite + vite-plugin-legacy ends up with the SDK default import undefined when run in the Edge emulator. Works fine when legacy plugin is disabled.

pat: Legacy plugin? That sounds like it might be injecting SystemJS/legacy wrappers. Can you share a tiny repro?

irene: Minimal repro (pnpm workspace):
1) packages/sdk/package.json -> {
  \"name\": \"@redwood/sdk\",
  \"version\": \"0.5.0\",
  \"main\": \"dist/index.cjs.js\",
  \"module\": \"dist/index.esm.js\",
  \"types\": \"dist/index.d.ts\"
}
2) packages/sdk/dist/index.esm.js -> export default function predict(){ return 'ok' }
3) apps/sample/vite.config.js -> plugins: [react(), legacy({ targets: [\"defaults\",\"IE 11\"] }), commonjs()] and build.target = 'es2018' for polyfill mix
4) apps/sample/src/edge.ts -> import predict from '@redwood/sdk'; add fetch handler that calls predict()

Observed: edge emu runtime error: TypeError: predict is not a function. Build contains legacy wrapper snippet and System.register-style chunk for the SDK. The final bundle exposes the SDK differently and the default import mapping isn't preserved.

olga: That's nasty. Legacy plugin will output transpiled chunks and sometimes wraps modules for older targets. Edge runtime expects modern ESM semantics; System.register wrappers break the loader's assumptions.

irene: Yep. Inspecting bundle: one chunk looks like System.register([...], function (exports) { return { setters:..., execute: function(){ exports('default', predict); } } }); but later the runtime doesn't execute the registration path we expect in the edge env, leaving the import unresolved. Sourcemap points to dist/index.cjs.js which is confusing.

pat: Quick fixes: (A) disable legacy plugin for edge build by gating it behind a browser-target env var, (B) prefer explicit package manifest exports so bundlers pick the modern ESM entry, (C) emit only ESM from the SDK and remove ambiguous `main` field.

olga: For DX I'd add (1) sampleapp templates that split build targets: modern (edge) vs legacy (browsers) and document toggling the plugin, (2) publish-lint to warn if package has main+module but no exports when both builds exist.

irene: I tried adding `exports": { "import": "dist/index.esm.js", "require": "dist/index.cjs.js" }` to the SDK package.json and disabling legacy for edge build. That fixed the runtime and sourcemaps now point to dist/index.esm.js.

pat: Nice. Also add a short note in devex onboarding: "If using vite-plugin-legacy, ensure edge builds run without legacy wrappers; prefer package.json exports pointing to ESM for edge-targeted packages."

olga: Action items: 1) irene will open a PR updating the sampleapp vite config to gate legacy plugin via env and add a comment explaining why. 2) Add publish-lint script in SDK CI to require exports when both module and main exist. 3) Add a lightweight CI smoke that builds sampleapp with legacy plugin enabled/disabled to catch regressions. 4) Add a short DevEx FAQ entry describing the legacy-plugin/edge mismatch and the `exports` snippet.

devex-bot: Ticket created DEVEX-2201: "vite-plugin-legacy causes default import loss for edge emu; recommend exports + gated legacy" (link: https://tracker.company/DEVEX-2201).

irene: I'll attach a tiny repro repo and include a one-line workaround: `import * as sdk from '@redwood/sdk'` works as a fallback but we should not ship sampleapps that require that.

pat: Agreed. Ship the explicit `exports` and gating approach in onboarding so new projects avoid this.

olga: Also add a note to the SDK publishing checklist: keep `types` in sync with `import` target in `exports` so sourcemaps and types resolve to ESM entry.

irene: PR opened with fixes and docs. Will follow up once CI smoke passes.
